question: Atlantic storms lasting two days or less rose from under one a year around 1900 to about five. What best explains it?
options: Warmer seas spawn more weak storms
Satellites and aircraft now spot them
Stronger El Niños cut storms short
answer: Satellites and aircraft now spot them. A storm that lived a day over open ocean in 1900 entered the record only if a ship happened to cross it. Landsea and colleagues found that storms lasting longer than two days show little rise over the same century. The brief ones blew and died unwatched.
move: Before trusting a rising count, ask whether the counting got better.
ask: Before I trust a rising count, have I asked whether the counting got better?
trap: Reading a longer list as a warmer ocean rather than sharper eyes.
source: Landsea et al., Journal of Climate, 2010
